definitions.explanation: External shutters on traditional Japanese houses that slide along tracks to protect windows from rain, storms, and intruders.

examples.japanese: ⟦{台風|たいふう}→台風：01455_taifuu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧{雨戸|あまど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{閉|し}めた→閉める：00485_shimeru⟧。
examples.english: I closed the storm shutters because a typhoon is coming.

examples.japanese: ⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なったら→なる：01970_naru⟧{雨戸|あまど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧。
examples.english: Open the storm shutters when morning comes.
Old houses have wooden storm shutters.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE: Traditional Japanese houses have {雨戸|あまど} that slide horizontally on tracks outside the windows. They are closed at night and during storms.

FUNCTIONS:
- Protection from rain and wind
- Security (closed at night)
- Insulation (keeps cold out)
- Privacy

MODERN VERSIONS:
- Electric/motorized shutters
- Roll-up shutters (⟦シャッター→シャッター：06380_shattaa⟧)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雨戸|あまど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ (to open shutters)
- {雨戸|あまど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{閉|し}める→閉める：00485_shimeru⟧ (to close shutters)
- {雨戸|あまど}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧ (to put up shutters)
